title: Random-forest selection links a food compound to COX-1 inhibition
summary: A random-forest model prioritized 5-methoxysalicylic acid for a COX-1 enzyme assay. It showed about 40% inhibition at 100 micromolar, whereas a higher-ranked single-fingerprint comparator did not inhibit at that concentration. This is a modest in-vitro target result, not evidence of dietary, therapeutic or clinical benefit.
organization: European Molecular Biology Laboratory; University of Cambridge

evidence.tested: An enzymatic assay compared the selected compound with positive and negative controls.
evidence.unknown: Cellular target engagement, efficacy and a robust compound IC50 are not established here.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest classification of drug-target similarity supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher abstract, selected model training and assay Results, publication date and affiliations; supplementary data not reviewed.
